saa-avc-230.text: An organization with dozens of accounts in AWS Organizations needs three corporate guarantees: prevent the use of unapproved regions, audit calls from API in all accounts and continuously evaluate the conformity of resource configurations in all accounts. What three mechanisms implement these guarantees? (Select THREE Alternatives))
options: Service Control Policies (SCPs) with regional condition applied to OWs
IAM Same policies manually copied for each account
An organization trail of CloudTrail covering all member accounts
Amazon GuardDuty as a record of audit of API
AWS Config with organizational aggregator and conformance packs in accounts
Disable the creation of new accounts
saa-avc-230.explanation: A) Correction: SCPs define the organisation's permission ceiling — the condition aws:RequestedRegion block Unapproved regions in TODAS the identity of the member accounts. B) Incorrect: manual copy is not governance — drifts and does not limit local admins. C) Correct: the organization trail records calls from API of all accounts at a central point. D) Incorrect: GuardDuty DETECTA threats using logs; who registers the audit is the CloudTrail. E) Correct: Config continuously evaluates the conformity of configurations, with aggregate view of the organization. F) Incorrect: preventing new accounts is not a compliance check.

saa-avc-231.text: A cluster Amazon EMR executes batch processing in night with flexible time. The team wants to drastically reduce the cost of computing, accepting occasional interruptions of us SEM lose data from HDFS. Which ones DUAS Do practices achieve this safely? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Use instances Spot in the knot TASK (not stored HDFS), keeping primary and core in On-Demand
Use instances Spot in TODOS the knots, including the primary
Adopt transient clusters: create the cluster for the job (data no S3 way EMRFS) and shut it down at the end
Keep the cluster on 24/7 to avoid bootstrap time
Fold the size of the core knots
saa-avc-231.explanation: A) Correct: we task only process — if Spot is taken, or YARN Reexecutes tasks in another node; core and primary are protected in On-Demand. B) Incorrect: lose primary in Spot drops the entire cluster; core in Spot risk data from HDFS. C) Correct: with data on S3 (EMRFS), the cluster becomes disposable: you only pay for the hours of the job. D) Incorrect: cluster 24/7 for night work is the waste that you want to eliminate. E) Incorrect: we increase the cost — the opposite of the objective.

saa-avc-232.text: Financial records recorded in S3 shall, by regulation, remain immutable by 7 years: neither administrators nor root user can alter or exclude them during retention. DUAS configurations implement this requirement WORM? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Enable S3 Object Lock in mode COMPLIANCE with retention period of 7 years
Enable S3 Object Lock in mode GOVERNANCE, which prevents changes even by root
Enable Bucket Version (Object Lock pre-requirement))
Apply a bucket policy denying s3:DeleteObject, which cannot be reversed
Use SSE-KMS, which makes objects immutable
saa-avc-232.explanation: A) Correct: compliance mode prevents exclusion/alteration by QUALQUER user, including root, until the end of retention — the WORM B) Incorrect: in governance mode, users with special permissions (s3:BypassGovernmentRetention) PODEM C) Correct: Object Lock requires enabled versioning in the pocket — both walk together. D) Incorrect: Bucket policies can always be changed by those who have permission (including root) — is not real immutability. E) Incorrect: encryption protects confidentiality, does not prevent exclusion.

saa-avc-233.text: One API serverless (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) has high latency in the first accesses after idle periods and degradation in repeated readings of DynamoDB at peak times. DUAS Do optimizations attack the two problems, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Configure Provided Competition in function Lambda to remove cold starters
Increase function timeout Lambda
Reduce function memory to speed up startup
Add or DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as read cache in microseconds
Change to API HTTP by REST
saa-avc-233.explanation: A) Correct: Provided Competition maintains pre-initialized run environments — the latency of the first access disappears. B) Incorrect: longer timeout only allows waiting longer; does not reduce latency. C) Incorrect: MENOS memory = less CPU = initialization and execution more LENTAS. D) Correct: or DAX is the native cache of DynamoDB — repeated readings begin to respond in microseconds, relieving the table in peaks. API does not resolve cold start or data cache.

saa-avc-234.text: A company wants a real-time near-analysis pipeline with the MENOR operational effort: application events should reach S3 already in Parquet, be discovered/catalogated automatically and be immediately consultable in SQL. WHAT THREE services make up this serverless pipeline? (Select THREE Alternatives)
options: Amazon Kinesis Firehose data with native conversion to Parquet and destination S3
A self-managed Kafka cluster in EC2
AWS Glue (crawler/Data Catalog) cataloging tables and partitions in S3
Amazon EC2 with cron conversion jobs
Amazon Athena running the consultations SQL directly on the S3
Amazon Neptune to store events
saa-avc-234.explanation: A) Correct: Firehose ingests, converts to Parquet and delivers no S3 no servers. B) Incorrect: Kafka in EC2 is the MAIOR possible operational effort for the same role. Glue discovers and maintains the catalogue (schemes/partitions) that the Athena use. D) Incorrect: EC2 + cron violates the serverless requirement and adds maintenance. Athena date or pipeline: SQL serverless direct at S3, F) Incorrect: Neptune is a graph bank — nothing to do with the scenario.

saa-avc-235.text: A company connects its datacenter to AWS by a single link Direct Connect and suffered a total interruption when he failed. The requirement now is hybrid connectivity RESILIENTE, with an automatic and encrypted backup path if the DX fails again. DUAS do measures make up the solution? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Add a second connection Direct Connect in a different location (location)
Configure a Site-to-Site VPN online as a backup route of the Direct Connect, how to fail away BGP
Add more VIFs to the same link Direct Connect
Use VPC Peering as DX backup
Switch DX to Public Internet with Elastic IPs
saa-avc-235.explanation: A) Correct: a second DX in distinct location eliminates the single point of physical failure — the most resilient option. B) Correct: a VPN Site-to-Site as backup gives an independent path (internet), encrypted, with automatic failure via BGP — the recommended design of balanced cost. C) Incorrect: more VIFs in MESMO link fall together with link. D) Incorrect: peering connects VPCs to each other — does not connect the datacenter. E) Incorrect: abandoning DX reduces the quality of connectivity instead of making it resilient.

saa-avc-236.text: The invoice of a VPC revealed high cost of NAT Gateway: cases EC2 in private sub-networks transfer dozens of TB/month to the Amazon S3 and the DynamoDB through the NAT. Which ones DUAS changes eliminate this transfer cost while maintaining private access? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for the S3 and adjust the route tables of private sub-networks
Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for the DynamoDB and adjust the route tables
Increase the number of NAT Gateways for sharing traffic
Move instances to public sub-networks
Compress the data before sending by NAT
saa-avc-236.explanation: A) Correct: the Gateway Endpoint of S3 It's GRATUITO and route traffic directly to service through the network of AWS — all this volume comes out of NAT. B) Correct: or DynamoDB is the other service with free Gateway Endpoint — the same economy. C) Incorrect: more NATs divide traffic, but the collection by processed GB remains the same (or greater, by overtime). D) Incorrect: expose the instances publicly exchange cost for security risk. E) Incorrect: compression reduces the volume a little bit, but keeps the architecture expensive — the endpoints zero this cost..
